submission:
I (28F) recently got engaged to my fiancé (30M), and we decided to have a small, intimate wedding ceremony with just our closest friends and family. We live in a small town, and my parents offered to host the reception at their home, which was incredibly generous. My parents have a beautiful backyard, so it seemed perfect for our low-key celebration.

Here's where things got complicated: My sister (31F) and her husband (33M) have been planning a big wedding for over a year. They booked a venue, hired a wedding planner, and have been sending out save-the-dates for a June wedding. My sister has been very vocal about how important it is for her to have her special day be a grand event, and I totally understand that. However, she completely flipped out when she learned about our wedding plans.

She accused me of stealing her thunder because our wedding is happening only a couple of weeks before hers. I tried to explain that we were not trying to compete with her, but she was having none of it. She even went as far as to say I should postpone my wedding to not overshadow hers. I didn't think that was fair, especially since my fiancé and I have been planning this for a much shorter time.

After a few heated conversations, she told me she refuses to come to my wedding, and her husband said he wouldn’t either if she wasn’t attending. I was really hurt, not just because I want her to be there, but also because I thought family should support each other, especially during significant life events.

Now, it's been a couple of weeks since our last argument, and I feel guilty about the whole situation. My parents are supportive of my wedding plans, but I can’t shake the feeling that I might be the bad guy for not accommodating my sister’s feelings. AITA for going ahead with my wedding as planned?

I'm (F) in my late 20s and recently got married to my husband (M), who has two kids from a previous relationship. We have been blending our families for about a year now, and overall, things have been going well. I genuinely care for my stepkids, and I try to involve them in our family activities as much as possible.

However, there's one issue that's been bothering me. My husband's ex-wife, who we'll call "Lisa," often invites herself to family events, and it's starting to feel uncomfortable. She's not just a little involved; she shows up at birthday parties, holidays, and even the occasional weekend outing we plan. At first, I thought it might be a good idea—keeping the peace for the kids' sake—but now I feel like I can't fully enjoy these moments as a new family. 

About a month ago, we planned a family outing to the zoo, just the five of us. I specifically told my husband that I wanted it to be a "just us" day. He agreed, but when we got there, Lisa showed up with the kids. I was caught off guard and ended up feeling overshadowed as she tried to take charge of the day, directing the kids and making decisions as if she were still the primary parent. 

I ended up speaking to my husband afterward, expressing that I felt uncomfortable with her constant presence and that it was affecting our family time. He got defensive, saying that Lisa is just trying to be involved in the kids' lives and that I should be more accommodating. I countered that I felt like I was losing my role in our family dynamic due to her interference. 

I might have been a bit harsh, but I told him that if this keeps happening, I would reconsider how I approach family activities. Now, he’s upset with me, saying that I’m trying to alienate the kids from their mother, and it's not fair to them. 

AITA for wanting some boundaries with my husband's ex-wife?

For context, I (F, 28) have a younger brother (M, 22) who just graduated and moved back in with our parents while he looks for a job. My family has always been supportive, especially of his interests in video games and streaming. I’ve been working in marketing for a few years now and have built a pretty successful career, so I’m financially independent.

Recently, my brother asked me if I could lend him my professional-grade camera for a project he was working on for his streaming channel. I’ve invested a lot into my camera equipment, and I use it for my freelance gigs. I explained that while I’m flattered he wants to use it, I need it for my work and can’t risk it being damaged or lost. He was visibly upset but said he’d figure something else out.

A few days later, I learned that he went ahead and borrowed our parents' camera without asking. It’s a lower-end model that’s not as reliable, and I was worried about how it would perform. I tried to be supportive and told him to make the most of it, but I couldn’t help but feel like he was undermining my boundaries.

Fast forward to yesterday, when I found out he had accidentally broken the camera while filming a stunt for his stream. He didn’t tell our parents because he was scared of what they’d say, but I found out through my mom, who was furious about how he handled it. Now our parents are upset with both of us—my brother for breaking the camera and me for not letting him use mine.

I confronted him and told him that if he had just respected my boundaries in the first place, he wouldn’t be in this mess. He called me a “selfish sister” and said I should’ve just lent him my camera if I really cared about him. Now, our family is divided, and I feel like I might be the bad guy here for not being more supportive.

AITA for refusing to lend my camera and for getting upset with my brother?

I (29F) recently went through a tough breakup with my boyfriend (30M) of three years. We had planned on moving in together, but when he called it quits, I had to quickly find a new place to live. Luckily, my friend (28F) offered me a room in her apartment while I got back on my feet. I really appreciated her generosity.

Things started off great, but soon, I noticed she would make comments about my cooking. I love to cook, and I tend to experiment with new recipes. The first time I made a spicy curry, she said, “Wow, that smells strong. Are you sure that’s a good idea?” I shrugged it off, but the comments kept coming. “Do you really think that’s healthy?” or “I guess some people like things like that.” 

I started to feel self-conscious about what I was making, but I tried not to let it get to me. Then, one evening, I made a big batch of homemade chili and invited her to join me. She accepted but when she took a bite, she immediately grimaced and said, “Wow, you must really like it spicy! I can’t handle this.” I didn’t take it personally; I offered her some sour cream to tone it down, but she just pushed her bowl away and said, “No thanks, I think I’ll just stick to my salad.”

The next day, I got a text from her saying she couldn’t keep living with me if I was going to keep cooking such “strong-smelling” food. I was taken aback. I understood that living in close quarters means being considerate, but I felt like she was being overly critical. I suggested we could work on a cooking schedule where I’d cook on certain days and she could stick to her salads on others, but she didn’t like that idea. 

Now, I’ve decided to look for a new place, but I’m starting to wonder if I’m the one in the wrong for cooking what I enjoy in her space. She’s been my friend for years, and I feel bad that it’s come to this. AITA for cooking what I like in my friend’s apartment?

I (29F) recently moved into a new apartment and have been super excited to finally have my own space. I’m a big fan of cooking, and I often try out new recipes that can get a bit messy. My best friend (30F) has been living in the area for a while and has always expressed her love for my cooking, often asking for me to make her stuff when she visits.

Last weekend, she asked if she could crash at my place for a couple of days since she was having some personal issues at home. I was more than happy to help her out, but I made it clear that my apartment is small and I needed her to be respectful of my space, especially since I was still unpacking and setting things up.

Things were going well until she started leaving her dishes piled up in the sink and taking my food without asking. I don’t mind sharing, but I think it’s important to ask first. I tried to be patient and just let it slide, but then I found my favorite cooking oil empty and she casually mentioned that she used it for a recipe she tried without telling me. 

On the third day, I planned to make a special dinner for us, but when I checked the fridge, I found that she had used most of my ingredients without asking. I was frustrated and confronted her about it. I told her that I appreciated her being here, but I felt like she was treating my place like it was her own without regard for my things. 

She got defensive and said I was being uptight and that friends share everything. Now she’s been giving me the cold shoulder, and I feel guilty for saying something, but I also think I deserve to have my space respected. 

So, AITA for calling out my friend for using my stuff without asking while she was staying at my place?

So, I (28F) have a younger brother, Jake (21M), who has recently started dating a girl named Sarah (20F). They’ve been together for about six months now, and while I think she’s sweet, I’ve noticed that she seems to be pretty insecure about their relationship. 

Jake is a laid-back guy who has a lot of friends, and he enjoys going out with them. Sarah, on the other hand, often gets anxious when he hangs out with friends without her. It’s not that he doesn’t want her to come; he just likes to maintain his own social life. Recently, I hosted a small gathering at my place, and Jake invited Sarah, but she declined, claiming she didn’t want to intrude on “family time.” 

During the gathering, I noticed Jake was receiving a lot of texts from her, and it seemed to distract him a bit. I overheard him telling her that he was busy with family, but she kept texting, and he eventually stepped outside to talk to her. I didn’t mind at first, but when he came back in, he looked frustrated. 

Later that night, Sarah sent him a message that was clearly meant to be a joke but came off as a little passive-aggressive. It was something like, “I hope you’re not having too much fun without me 😉.” Jake rolled his eyes and showed it to me, clearly annoyed. I jokingly said, "Well, maybe she should lighten up a bit," and he just sighed. 

Now, here’s where I might have crossed a line. I sent Sarah a message on Instagram (we follow each other) and told her that I thought she was being a bit too clingy and that Jake deserves to have his own space. I thought I was helping, but now Jake is upset with me, saying that I should have stayed out of it and that this was a conversation he needed to have with her himself.

I didn’t mean to overstep, but I thought it might help their relationship. My parents think I should apologize to Jake, but I honestly feel like I might have been right in some way. AITA for messaging my brother’s girlfriend about their relationship?

For context, I (F, 28) recently moved into a new apartment after getting a promotion at work. I’m excited to finally have my own space and have been putting a lot of effort into making it feel like home. A couple of weeks ago, I hosted a small housewarming party with a few friends and some neighbors. It was a great night, and everyone seemed to have fun.

One of my neighbors (M, 30) who I hadn't interacted much with before showed up unexpectedly. He seemed to enjoy the party and even offered to help with setting up and cleaning afterward. I thought it was nice and appreciated his help, but I didn’t think much of it at the time. 

A few days later, he knocked on my door and asked if I wanted to join him for dinner sometime. I thought it could be a nice way to get to know him better, so I agreed. We ended up having a good time, and he even helped me assemble some furniture the next week. 

However, things took a turn when he started getting a bit too comfortable. He began dropping by unannounced, sometimes just to hang out or to borrow things. At first, I didn’t mind too much, but it quickly became overwhelming. I’m a pretty private person and value my alone time, and it felt like he was crossing a line.

I finally had to set boundaries. I told him that while I appreciate his friendship, I need some space and prefer to plan visits ahead of time. He seemed taken aback and said that he thought we were becoming good friends. I felt bad for hurting his feelings, but I knew I had to be honest.

Since then, he has been distant and has even suggested that I’m being unfriendly or standoffish. I’ve heard from other neighbors that he’s been telling them I’m rude and ungrateful. I’m starting to feel guilty for wanting my privacy and setting boundaries. 

So, AITA for telling my neighbor I need space after he started dropping by unannounced?

I (30F) recently got married to my partner (32M) after dating for five years. We had a small wedding ceremony with close friends and family, and it was a beautiful day. However, there's been a lot of drama surrounding the event, mainly because of my sister (28F).

To give you some context, my sister and I have always had a rocky relationship. She's the type to be competitive about everything, and it seems like she feels overshadowed by me. When I got engaged, she made a big deal about how she wanted to get married first. I didn’t think much of it at the time but her comments started to get more intense leading up to my wedding.

During the planning process, she constantly "subtly" reminded me of how she was still single and how much she wanted a wedding. I tried to be supportive, even encouraging her to date more actively, but it felt like everything was about her and her frustrations. 

On the day of my wedding, she showed up wearing a bright white dress that was nearly identical to mine. I was shocked. It was beyond inappropriate, and I felt like she was trying to upstage me. During the ceremony, she kept making snide comments under her breath, and I could see her rolling her eyes while I was saying my vows. Afterward, I confronted her about the dress and her behavior. I told her that it was really hurtful and that I didn't appreciate her trying to make my day about her.

She ended up storming off, and my parents were furious with me, saying I should have "let it go" because she’s going through a tough time. They think I should apologize to her for confronting her instead of enjoying my wedding day. I feel like I had every right to stand up for myself and my special day, but now I'm feeling guilty because my family's upset with me.

AITA for confronting my sister about her behavior on my wedding day?

I (30F) recently found myself in a pretty uncomfortable situation with my older sister (35F). We grew up in a large family, and my sister has always been the overachiever, which I really admire. She’s always had a great job, a nice house, and a seemingly perfect life. I’m still trying to find my footing career-wise and have struggled with serious anxiety and depression for years.

For context, I recently got a promotion at my job, which I was incredibly proud of, but I don’t think it measures up to my sister’s achievements in her eyes. When I told her about the promotion, her response was pretty lukewarm. She congratulated me but quickly transitioned to talking about her recent promotion and how she’s now managing a huge project at work. I felt a bit deflated, but I brushed it off.

Last week, we had a family gathering, and I was excited to share my news with everyone. My sister was there, and as soon as I mentioned my promotion, she rolled her eyes and said, “That’s cute, but you know promotions aren’t everything, right? It’s about the impact you make.” In front of everyone! I was embarrassed and hurt. I tried to laugh it off, but I felt really small.

That night, I confronted her privately. I told her that her comments were disrespectful and that I wanted her to recognize my accomplishments instead of belittling them. She got defensive and accused me of being overly sensitive. She said that I should be grateful for what I have and not expect everyone to throw a party for every little win. 

I’m still upset about the whole thing. I’ve been contemplating whether I overreacted or if I was justified in my feelings. My parents think I should just let it go and not escalate things, but I feel like she needs to understand how her words affect me. 

AITA for confronting my sister about her dismissive remarks?

I (28F) recently had a pretty heated disagreement with my sister (32F) and now I'm left wondering if I went too far. 

For some context, our parents always made a big deal about family gatherings, especially for birthdays and holidays. Last month, I planned a surprise birthday party for my sister, which I thought would be a great way to celebrate her. I coordinated with our parents, invited her close friends, and even ordered her favorite cake. 

When she walked in and saw everyone, she was genuinely surprised and seemed to be happy at first. But then, about an hour into the party, she started complaining about how I didn’t consult her before planning the event, saying she wasn’t ready to celebrate and that she preferred something more low-key this year. I was taken aback because I thought I was doing something nice for her.

She started picking apart every detail, from the decorations to the guest list. I tried to explain that I wanted to do something special for her, but she just wouldn’t let it go. Eventually, in the heat of the moment, I snapped and said, “You know, it’s not like we’re always throwing you parties; I thought you’d appreciate this one instead of being so ungrateful!” 

Her face fell, and she walked away to talk to our parents, who sided with her, saying I should have respected her wishes, even if she didn’t express them clearly. After that, the party pretty much fizzled out, and it felt awkward. 

Now, I’m feeling guilty about how I reacted. I thought I was being considerate, but maybe I was being selfish by wanting to throw her a party that I thought she should want. AITA for losing my temper and saying those things?

So I (F, 28) recently moved in with my boyfriend (M, 30) after dating for about a year. We both agreed to split the rent and household expenses evenly, which I thought was fair since we both make about the same amount of money. However, things took a turn last month when my boyfriend suggested that I start paying for groceries as well. 

At first, I didn’t think much of it and agreed, but when I noticed he was making some extravagant meals that I wouldn’t necessarily buy myself, I started to feel uncomfortable. I mean, I’m fine with contributing to a shared grocery budget, but I didn’t want to be the primary buyer for elaborate meals that he wanted to cook. So, I suggested that we set a budget for groceries and stick to it, asking him to choose recipes that fit within that budget.

He got really defensive and said that if I didn’t want to contribute more to the meals he was excited to cook, then I could just eat what I bought for myself. I felt that was unfair because we’re living together, and I thought part of sharing a home meant sharing meals as well. We ended up having a pretty heated discussion about it, and at one point I told him that I didn’t appreciate his cooking being treated like a luxury.

Now, I feel like I may have overstepped. He loves cooking and I guess I unintentionally made him feel unappreciated. Since then, he’s been giving me the cold shoulder, saying I don’t understand his passion for cooking. I’ve tried apologizing for how I approached the conversation, but he insists that I was dismissive of something he values. 

AITA for wanting to set a grocery budget and express my concerns about the costs associated with his cooking?

I (29F) have a younger sister (23F) who is getting married next month. She and her fiancé are planning a big wedding, and while I’m excited for her, I’ve been feeling a bit overwhelmed by all the responsibilities that seem to be falling on me. My sister has always been a bit of a perfectionist, and she tends to get stressed out easily, which means I’ve stepped in as her “calm” support person for a lot of the wedding planning.

Here’s where it gets tricky: a few weeks ago, she asked me to help her with her wedding budget, which was already ballooning beyond what they initially planned. I pointed out that they should consider cutting back on some things, including the extravagant centerpieces and the fancy venue. She didn’t like the idea of downsizing and insisted that it was her big day and she wanted it to be perfect. I completely understood that but reminded her that they should not start their marriage in debt.

Fast forward to last weekend. My sister and her fiancé were having a big family gathering to celebrate their upcoming nuptials, and I was tasked with helping out with the food. While I was prepping, I overheard her talking to a couple of her friends about how she wanted to surprise everyone with a choreographed dance for the reception. It sounded amazing, but I couldn’t help but think about how much time and money that would require. 

Later that evening, I gently brought it up with her, suggesting that maybe they could save the dance for their first anniversary instead. She blew up at me, saying that I was ruining her excitement and that I just didn’t understand how important this was to her and her fiancé.

After the gathering, she called me crying, saying she felt like I was trying to control her wedding and that I was being a “Debbie Downer.” I was shocked. I thought I was just being practical, but now I’m questioning if I crossed a line. I want her to have her dream wedding, but I also want her to be realistic about finances. 

So, AITA for trying to help my sister be practical about her wedding plans?

I (28F) recently moved out of my parents’ house and into my first apartment. It’s a small one-bedroom and I’m really excited about it. My parents have always been very supportive, but they’re also pretty controlling. My mom especially has a habit of wanting to “help” with everything, which usually means she shows up unannounced and takes over.

A few weeks ago, my mom called and said she wanted to come over to help me decorate. I really appreciated the offer, but I also wanted to do it on my own. I told her thanks but that I was excited to do it myself and that I had everything planned out. She seemed fine with that, or so I thought.

Fast forward to last weekend, my mom surprise visits me while I’m at work. I get home and find my entire living room rearranged, new curtains hung, and decorations all over the place. I was shocked. I felt like I’d lost my space. I know she meant well, but it was so overwhelming. I tried to hide my frustration, but I couldn’t help asking why she did this without my permission.

She got defensive and said she just wanted to help and that I should be grateful since I’m “just a young girl who doesn’t know how to decorate.” I told her I didn’t want her to do that and felt like she disregarded my wishes. We ended up having a big argument, and she left in tears.

Now my dad is upset with me, saying I should have appreciated her effort and that I’m being ungrateful. I feel bad for hurting her feelings but at the same time, I don’t think I’m in the wrong for wanting to make my own choices about my space. AITA for being upset with my mom for decorating my apartment without my consent?

I'm a 28-year-old woman and I’ve been working at my job for about four years. I got promoted to a managerial position last year and I take my responsibilities seriously. Recently, our team had a big project deadline, and due to some unexpected complications, we had to put in a lot of extra hours to get things done. I ended up working late for about two weeks straight, and while I pushed my team to do their best, I always made sure to recognize their hard work.

Last week, after we finally met the deadline, we had a team celebration planned. I’d arranged for pizza and drinks to thank everyone for their effort. However, one of my team members, “Tom,” who’s been with the company for about a year, showed up late and immediately started criticizing my management style in front of everyone, saying I was too demanding and made unnecessary changes that delayed the project. I was taken aback because this was supposed to be a celebratory event, not a public forum for complaints.

After the gathering, I pulled Tom aside and asked him why he chose that moment to air his grievances. He told me he felt it was important to express his opinions and that maybe I could learn from his feedback. I calmly explained that while I value constructive criticism, there’s a time and place for everything, and that wasn’t it. I also mentioned that I felt disrespected and that his comments could have negatively impacted team morale.

Tom didn't take it well and accused me of being overly sensitive. He said he was just trying to help and that I should be open to feedback regardless of the setting. Since then, he's been distant, and a few of my other team members have also mentioned feeling uncomfortable with how I handled the situation. I’m starting to feel guilty, wondering if I overreacted by confronting him directly and telling him to be more respectful. 

AITA for calling Tom out in front of the team and telling him he was out of line?

I (28F) recently got married, and my husband (30M) and I decided to have a small wedding with close family and friends due to budget constraints and a desire for intimacy. We both agreed on a guest list of about 50 people, and we were excited to celebrate this special day without the stress of a massive ceremony.

A few weeks before the wedding, my sister (32F) reached out to tell me she was pregnant and due two weeks after my wedding date. While I was super happy for her, I also found out she wanted to bring her partner and their son (3M) to the wedding. I love my sister, but the thought of adding more guests, especially in the context of her pregnancy and a toddler, stressed me out. I gently explained that we’ve already finalized our guest list, and I hoped she’d understand that we wanted to keep it small and intimate.

Instead of understanding, she got really upset and accused me of not caring about her family. She insisted that family should come first and that I was being selfish for not wanting to include her. I felt awful, but I held my ground and said that the decision was made, and I couldn't change the number of guests at this point without compromising our original vision for the day.

Fast forward to the wedding day, she showed up anyway with her partner and son, who was running around and making a scene during the ceremony. It was chaotic, and I was really frustrated because I had asked her not to come. After the ceremony, I confronted her and told her that I felt disrespected by her decision to come despite my request. We ended up arguing, and she stormed off, saying I was being an awful sister.

Now, I feel guilty because I love her and want to support her, but I also think she crossed a boundary. My parents are split on the issue; my mom thinks I should have just let it slide since it was a family event, but my dad agrees with me that I set a boundary that she ignored.

AITA for telling my sister she couldn’t come to my wedding?

For context, I (28F) have a younger sister (24F) who recently got engaged to her boyfriend (26M). They've been dating for about two years now, and while I think he's a nice guy, I’ve noticed some concerning habits that I can't help but mention.

My sister is an artist and has always been passionate about her work, but since getting engaged, she's been talking about how she wants to make her fiancé happy and has started to prioritize his needs over her own aspirations. I tried to be supportive at first, but I noticed she was neglecting her own art shows and freelance opportunities to accommodate his schedule and interests.

Last week, my sister invited me to lunch to celebrate her engagement and mentioned how she wanted to cancel her upcoming art exhibition because her fiancé had planned a weekend trip for them. I expressed my concern, saying that I didn’t think it was a good idea to put her fiancé's plans before something she was excited about. I told her that her art is important and that she shouldn't feel obligated to drop everything for him.

She got upset and accused me of being jealous of her relationship. I didn't mean to come off as jealous; I genuinely wanted her to stay true to herself. She then told me that maybe I just didn’t understand what it was like to be in love and that I was being unsupportive. I left the lunch feeling frustrated and unsure if I crossed a line.

A couple of days later, she posted on social media about how excited she was for the trip, and I felt like a jerk for saying anything. Our parents think I should apologize to her for my "interference," but I can't help but feel like I was looking out for her well-being.

AITA for trying to encourage my sister to prioritize her art over her fiancé’s plans?

So, I've been living in my apartment (F, 28) for about three years now, and I have a pretty good relationship with my neighbors, especially the couple next door (let's call them Jake and Sarah). They’re friendly, and we often chat when we run into each other. 

A few weeks ago, I noticed that they had a "For Sale" sign in their yard. I didn’t think much of it at first, just assumed they were looking for a change. But then, last week, I overheard them talking in the hallway about how they would be moving out in a month. I casually mentioned to them that I really loved the way they decorated their place and that I’d be sad to see them go, especially since they were such great neighbors. 

Now here’s where things get a bit complicated. They told me they were selling their furniture, and since they’d be moving out soon, they wanted to give me first dibs on anything I might want. I was excited! They have some really nice pieces, and I’ve been wanting to upgrade my current furniture for a while. 

We agreed on prices for a few items, and I arranged to pick them up this weekend. However, as I was getting ready to help them move the furniture out, I overheard them talking about their plans to move to a house in the suburbs and how much they were looking forward to having a bigger space for their kids. 

Then it hit me. My twin sister (F, 26) is currently renting a room in a not-so-great area, and she’s been looking for a place to live. I thought to myself, "What if I ask Jake and Sarah if they’d be willing to let my sister rent their place after they move out?" 

I brought it up casually while we were packing up the furniture. They seemed a bit surprised but said they’d consider it. I was excited, thinking this could be a perfect solution for my sister, and it would keep good neighbors in the building.

But later that night, I got a text from Jake saying they had decided to go ahead and list the apartment for rent through a real estate agent. I felt really bad because I thought I might have overstepped by suggesting my sister and I hadn’t meant to pressure them. 

Now I’m feeling guilty. I didn't mean to put them in an awkward position, and I know they have the right to choose what to do

For context, I'm a (29F) nurse in a busy city hospital, and I’ve been working night shifts for the past three years. My best friend (28F) is also a nurse but works day shifts. Recently, we both got a weekend off together, and I was super excited to finally hang out, especially since I’ve been feeling burnt out at work.

We decided to plan a little getaway to a nearby beach resort. I booked the hotel room and paid for most of the expenses upfront, with the understanding that she would cover her half once we arrived. I was excited to enjoy some sun and relaxation, but when we got there, I noticed that she was acting a bit differently.

On the first night, she insisted on going out for dinner, which I didn’t mind, but I suggested a place that was more budget-friendly, given that I had already spent quite a bit on the trip. She pushed back and insisted on a fancier restaurant, saying, “We deserve this!” I agreed, but I was starting to feel uneasy about the expenses. 

After dinner, when the bill came, she ordered an extra appetizer and a dessert and then looked at me expectantly. I ended up covering the bill, thinking it was just one night and hoping she would pitch in later. The next day, she wanted to do a spa day, which was fine, but again, she suggested a high-end spa that was way out of our budget. I hesitated but ultimately went along with it, thinking it’d be a fun experience.

By the end of the weekend, I had paid for nearly everything—a total that far exceeded what we had initially planned. I was frustrated but didn’t want to ruin our time, so I kept my mouth shut until we got back home. When I finally brought it up, she was defensive and said it was “just a vacation” and that I shouldn’t be so uptight about money. I felt that I was taken advantage of, especially since we had discussed splitting costs beforehand.

Now, she’s upset with me for bringing it up and says I’m ruining our friendship over a “fun trip.” I don’t want to hold a grudge, but I also feel like I shouldn’t have to foot the bill for her extravagant choices. AITA for calling her out on this?

I (32F) recently got married, and my husband (34M) and I decided to have a small wedding with just close friends and family. We wanted to keep it intimate and personal, so we opted for a backyard ceremony at my parents’ house.

My sister (29F) has been dating her boyfriend (30M) for about a year. While I don’t have any issues with him, my sister has a habit of being dramatic and making everything about her. Leading up to the wedding, she kept mentioning how she wished she could have a "big fairy tale wedding" someday. I understood she had her dreams, but I reminded her that this day wasn’t about her. 

On the day of the wedding, everything was going smoothly until it was time for the vows. My sister's boyfriend, who had been drinking, suddenly stood up and made a toast about how my sister deserves the best wedding ever and how she should be the one in a white dress. It caught everyone off guard, and I could see my sister beaming like she was the bride. I was taken aback but tried to brush it off.

After the ceremony, my sister cornered me and started crying, saying that her boyfriend’s speech was a sign that she should have a wedding like mine. She accused me of stealing her spotlight and being selfish for not including her in planning my special day. I was genuinely confused and tried to explain that it was never my intention to overshadow her dreams. My parents supported me, but my sister continued to argue, saying I was the one being insensitive.

Now I'm feeling torn. I didn’t want to hurt her feelings, but at the same time, I feel like I have every right to celebrate my wedding the way I wanted. AITA for not accommodating my sister’s feelings during my wedding?

I (F, 29) recently got engaged to my boyfriend (M, 32) after a whirlwind romance that we both feel is right. We’re planning a small wedding in my hometown, where I’ve lived my entire life, but we agreed to have a destination honeymoon instead to avoid the stress of a big wedding. 

Here’s where the problem started: my best friend, “Sara” (F, 30), and I have been inseparable since childhood. When I told her about the engagement, she was over the moon and we started discussing wedding plans. I mentioned that I didn’t want a big wedding, and she was supportive—until I offhandedly mentioned that I wanted to do a small guest list with just close family and friends. 

She then suggested that I should just have a bigger wedding because “you only get married once” and that I should go all out. I explained that I wanted to keep it intimate and meaningful. Sara seemed to get upset and accused me of not wanting her there, which completely took me by surprise. I assured her that she would be invited but that I felt overwhelmed by the idea of a big event.

A few weeks later, I found out from another friend that Sara was telling people in our circle that I was “selfish” for not wanting a big wedding and that I was “excluding” her for my choices. I confronted her about it, and she doubled down on her feelings, saying I was being short-sighted and that it was “all about me” and “not thinking of what a wedding should be.” 

I tried to compromise by suggesting we could have a larger reception afterward, where I could invite more friends, but she just got angrier, saying it’s not the same and I should just throw everything I want aside for everyone else. 

Feeling frustrated and hurt, I told her that it’s my wedding and I have the right to choose how I want to celebrate it. Now, she’s refusing to speak to me and has told some mutual friends that I’m an “asshole” for not considering her feelings. 

I feel torn because I truly value our friendship but don’t think I did anything wrong by wanting to keep my wedding small. AITA for wanting a small wedding and not wanting to bend to my friend’s expectations?

I (29F) recently had a falling out with my sister (27F) over her wedding plans, and now I'm wondering if I overstepped my bounds. For context, I was a bridesmaid in her wedding, and she’s always been a bit of a perfectionist, which is fine, but this time she seems to be taking it to another level.

She wanted a very extravagant wedding, and I totally understand wanting your special day to be memorable. However, she came to me a few weeks ago and asked if I could help her with some expenses because she was going over budget. I felt bad for her but also knew she had some financial choices that led to this situation, like booking a venue that was much more expensive than she initially planned.

After some thought, I agreed to lend her a significant amount of money, but I laid down some boundaries. I told her that I wouldn’t contribute to anything that I felt was unnecessary, like the fancy centerpieces or the elaborate dessert table. We shook on it, and I felt good about supporting her.

Fast forward to last weekend, I was at her place helping her with some wedding crafts. I noticed she had ordered a ridiculously overpriced wedding cake that was way above what we discussed. When I confronted her about it, she got defensive and told me it was her wedding and she could do what she wanted. I reminded her of our agreement, and she said I was being unsupportive and that I needed to trust her judgment.

Things escalated quickly, and I ended up telling her that if she was going to ignore our agreement and blow my money on things that weren't necessary, then maybe she didn't deserve my help at all. She ended up in tears, saying I was ruining her happiness and that I should be excited for her instead of judging her choices.

I feel guilty because I don't want to hurt her, but I also believe there's a line when it comes to financial responsibility. Now, she’s not talking to me, and my family is divided on who’s in the wrong. AITA for standing my ground and questioning her spending?

I (28F) recently had an argument with my brother (25M) that left me questioning if I was in the wrong. For context, our family has always been pretty close, but there’s been a noticeable shift since he got engaged to his fiancé (25F) six months ago. I fully support their relationship and am excited for their future, but I’ve noticed that he has become increasingly dismissive of my opinions and feelings since they started planning their wedding.

A few weeks ago, I was invited to help them with some wedding planning. During the discussion, I brought up the idea of having a smaller ceremony, as I thought it would be more intimate and less stressful for them. My brother laughed and said something like, “That’s cute, but we’re going big or going home.” I felt a bit hurt since I was trying to offer my support, and I told him it seemed like he was prioritizing a show over the actual commitment. He brushed this off, saying, “You wouldn’t understand; it’s not your wedding.”

After that, things went downhill fast. I tried to suggest a few budget-friendly ideas for the reception, and he cut me off, saying they had already decided on everything and I should just stick to being a guest. I lost my temper and told him that if he didn’t want my help, he should have just said so instead of pretending he valued my input. He got defensive and accused me of being jealous and trying to sabotage their happiness.

Now, I feel like the bad guy. My parents are somewhat on his side, saying I should have been more supportive, and I should just let them do what they want. But I feel like I was just trying to help, and he completely shut me down. I even considered stepping back from the wedding entirely. 

So, AITA for wanting to voice my opinion and being upset when he dismissed me?

For context, I'm a 27-year-old woman living in a small apartment in the city. I recently got a promotion at work that requires me to travel a lot, which is exciting but also means I’m away from home for extended periods. 

My best friend, “Amy,” who is 28, has been struggling to find stable work since the pandemic. She’s been living paycheck to paycheck, and I can see how stressed she is. A week ago, she reached out and asked if she could stay with me for a month while she looks for a job. I hesitated but ultimately agreed, thinking it would help her get back on her feet and would be good for both of us.

I explained to her that I have a pretty minimal setup. I only have one bedroom, and I work from home when I’m not traveling, so it would be a little cramped. She assured me it would be fine, and she would try to stay out of my way.

The first few days went okay, but then things started to get tricky. She’s been using my things without asking—like my food, my laptop charger, and even my shampoo. I don’t mind sharing, but I feel like she’s taking advantage of my hospitality. She also has a habit of leaving my place a mess, which I can’t stand since I like to keep my space tidy, especially when I’m working.

Yesterday, I came back from a week of travel and found my apartment in disarray. Dishes were piled up, things were strewn everywhere, and she was watching TV with the volume blasting. When I asked her about it, she brushed it off, saying she was just trying to relax since she had a few interviews coming up.

After a long day, I snapped a bit and told her that if she couldn’t respect my space, she would need to find somewhere else to stay. Now she’s upset and saying I’m being unsupportive during a tough time for her. I feel bad, but I also think I deserve to have my home treated with respect. 

AITA for telling my friend she needs to leave if she can’t keep my space tidy?

For context, I (F, 28) recently got engaged to my fiancé (M, 30). We’re both very excited, but there’s been some unexpected tension between my fiancé and my sister (F, 25) that I can't shake off. My sister has always been a bit dramatic, but this time feels different.

When I got engaged, my sister was initially thrilled and even offered to help plan the wedding. However, it all took a turn when I asked her to be my maid of honor. She agreed, but then started making suggestions that felt more like demands. For example, she insisted on choosing the venue and my dress without considering my input. I tried to compromise, but she often dismissed my ideas as "boring" or "too simple."

Last week, while discussing the wedding guest list, my sister suggested we not invite some of my fiancé's closest friends because "they're not our type." I found this pretty disrespectful and told her that the guest list should include people who matter to us, not just who she approves of. That's when she exploded, saying I was being ungrateful and that she was just trying to help make the wedding "stylish."

Feeling overwhelmed, I told her I needed some space, and for the last few days, I’ve barely talked to her. My parents are caught in the middle and have said I should make up with my sister because "family comes first." They think I’m being too harsh and that I should let her have some control over the wedding planning since she’s so passionate about it.

So, AITA for stepping back from my sister and standing up for what I want in my own wedding?

I (29F) recently got engaged to my fiancé (31M), and we’re quite excited about planning our wedding. We’ve both been looking forward to this moment, but there’s a bit of a complication. 

My best friend, “Samantha” (30F), has been in a long-term relationship with her boyfriend (32M) for a few years now. They’ve talked about getting married, but they haven’t set a date yet. Samantha has always been super supportive of my relationship, and I thought the same would go for my wedding. 

However, when I shared the news about my engagement, she seemed strangely distant. I thought she might just need time to adjust, but over the next few weeks, her reaction didn’t improve. She would often change the subject when I brought up wedding plans or just look visibly upset. Finally, I asked her what was wrong. 

She confessed that she feels like I’m “stealing her thunder” by getting engaged before she does. I was taken aback; I never intended to overshadow her! I’ve always encouraged her to get engaged when she felt ready, but she believes that since we’re close friends, I should have waited until she got engaged first. 

I told her that I can’t control when I get engaged and that I’ve been waiting for this moment for a long time. I offered to include her in the wedding planning process—like having her be my maid of honor—but she said it wouldn’t make a difference. Now, she’s been avoiding me and hasn’t responded to my texts, and I feel like I’ve lost my best friend over this. I’m heartbroken that she feels this way, but I also feel like I’m not the one in the wrong here.

I (28F) recently had a fight with my sister (30F) over a family vacation that’s been planned for months. We’ve been looking forward to it as a way to reconnect after a rocky couple of years. The plan was to rent a cabin in the mountains for a long weekend, and everyone contributed to the costs, including my parents. 

A week before we were set to leave, my sister texted me and our parents, saying she couldn’t go anymore because she was feeling overwhelmed with work and needed to save money for some unexpected expenses. I totally understood where she was coming from, and I told her it was okay. But then she asked if I could cover her share of the cabin rental since she was bailing at the last minute. I was taken aback. I’d already budgeted for the trip, and it felt unfair to put that burden on me, especially since I had already said I understood her reasons for not coming.

I told her I wasn’t comfortable covering her share, especially since I had other obligations to pay for. I suggested that she could still come if she was willing to at least pay her part, but I’d be okay if she couldn’t swing it. That’s when things got heated. She accused me of being unsupportive and not understanding how hard it is to juggle everything. She also said that if I was really her sister, I’d help her out.

I’ve always been the one to support her, whether it was financially or emotionally, so this felt like a slap in the face. I told her that I was disappointed that she couldn’t prioritize family time over work for once. After that, she stopped responding to my messages, and our parents are now caught in the middle, trying to mediate.

Now I’m feeling really guilty about the whole situation. I didn’t mean to escalate things, but I also don’t think I should have to shoulder her financial responsibilities. AITA for not covering my sister's share of the cabin rental?

For context, I'm a 28-year-old woman and I live with my boyfriend (29) in a small apartment. We’ve been together for about two years, and while we get along well most of the time, there’s one issue that’s been bothering me.

I’ve always been passionate about cooking and enjoy trying out new recipes. I usually cook dinner most nights and love experimenting with different cuisines. However, my boyfriend has a very specific palate and is not as adventurous when it comes to food. He prefers simple meals—think chicken, rice, and broccoli. I’ve tried to introduce him to new flavors, but he often turns his nose up and insists on ordering takeout instead.

Last week, after a long day at work, I decided to make a new Thai curry recipe I found. I spent a couple of hours prepping and cooking, and I was really excited about it. When I finally served it, he took one look at it and made a face. He said, “I’m not really in the mood for that. Can we just order pizza instead?” I felt completely deflated. I didn’t even want to eat the curry anymore, and we ended up ordering pizza, which felt like a waste of all the time and effort I had put into cooking.

Feeling frustrated, I told him that I was tired of feeling like my cooking wasn’t appreciated. I reminded him that I enjoy cooking and that I put a lot of love into it. He responded by saying I was being dramatic and should just accept that he doesn't like the same food I do. I was hurt and ended up storming off to the bedroom.

A few days later, after a bit of reflection, I decided to talk to him about how I felt. I suggested we could take turns choosing meals each week—he picks one, I pick one—so we both have a say in what we eat. He agreed but then said I was being a bit of a diva for getting so upset about one meal.

Now I’m left wondering if I overreacted. AITA for being upset about him not liking my cooking and wanting to find a compromise?

So I (F, 27) recently got engaged to my partner (M, 29) after three years of dating. We both come from different cultural backgrounds, and while our families get along, there are some traditions that we want to incorporate into our wedding. This is where things have gotten complicated.

My fiancé’s family has a significant tradition of a “family blessing” ceremony that is very important to them. It involves a large gathering of close family members where they do a sort of group blessing for the couple. On the other hand, my family has a custom of not including extended family in wedding events unless they’re directly related to the couple, which means my parents have expressed they prefer a smaller, more intimate ceremony with just immediate family.

We’ve been trying to find a compromise. We thought about having two separate events: one for my family and one for his. However, my fiancé’s parents are insistent that all family must be invited to the blessing, which would mean a much larger event and potentially a lot of people I don’t know. My parents are also not comfortable with the idea of a big, crowded gathering, especially since they feel it detracts from the intimacy of the occasion.

Tensions reached a boiling point last week when we had a heated discussion about the guest list. My fiancé accused me of not valuing his family’s traditions and being selfish about my own. I tried to explain that it’s not about valuing one over the other but about wanting to create a day that feels right for both of us. In response, he suggested that I was being unreasonable and unwilling to compromise. 

After that argument, I decided to take a step back and said I would consider his family’s feelings more, but I also told him that if we don’t find a middle ground, I would prefer to just elope rather than do something that makes both of us uncomfortable. This didn’t go over well, and now he’s saying I’m being dramatic and that I’m making the planning process miserable.

Now I’m feeling guilty because I love him and want our wedding to be special for both of us, but I also don’t want to feel overwhelmed and pressured into a situation that doesn’t reflect what we both want. AITA for suggesting we just elope if we can’t find a compromise?

So, I (F, 28) have been living with my boyfriend (M, 30) for about a year now, and we recently adopted a dog together. We both love animals and were excited about the new addition to our home. However, I’ve noticed that my boyfriend has a pretty laid-back approach to training and discipline, while I tend to be more structured and consistent.

The issue really came to a head last week. Our dog, Max, is still a puppy and has a tendency to chew on things he shouldn't. One day, while I was out running errands, my boyfriend let Max roam free in our apartment. When I returned, I found that Max had chewed through the corner of our couch and a pair of my favorite shoes. I was understandably upset and confronted my boyfriend about it. 

He shrugged it off and said, “He’s just a puppy; he’ll grow out of it.” I explained that we need to set boundaries and consequences for his behavior, but he insisted that it was too harsh to discipline him. I ended up raising my voice a bit, which is something I rarely do. I told him that if he couldn't take the training seriously, maybe I should be the one to take care of Max since I was clearly more invested in his well-being.

Things escalated, and my boyfriend got defensive, saying I was overreacting and that I was making him feel like a bad pet owner. After a few days of not talking much, I finally suggested we sit down and discuss the situation calmly. He agreed, but I can tell he’s still upset about how I handled it initially.

Now, I’m wondering if I went too far by raising my voice and suggesting he shouldn’t be involved in Max’s care. He’s a great partner in many ways, but when it comes to the dog, I feel like I’m alone in my concerns. AITA for how I reacted?

For context, I (F, 28) recently got engaged to my boyfriend (M, 30) of five years. We’ve been living together for the past two years and have been planning our wedding for the next year. I come from a close-knit family, and we often gather for special occasions. My boyfriend, on the other hand, has a more complicated family situation. His parents divorced when he was a teenager, and his relationship with both of them is strained.

When we announced our engagement, I was excited to share the news with my family. To my surprise, my boyfriend asked if we could keep the engagement a secret for a while, saying he wasn’t ready to share it with his family. I respected his wishes but found it odd since I always thought that sharing such a happy moment should be a joint celebration.

Fast forward a couple of weeks later, and my parents planned a big family dinner to celebrate our engagement. I invited my boyfriend to join us, but he declined, saying he wasn’t comfortable in such settings. I understood, but I couldn’t help but feel disappointed. I ended up going without him, and my family was thrilled to celebrate with me.

During the dinner, my sister (F, 25) commented on how happy she was for me and started asking about the wedding plans. I mentioned a few ideas, and before I knew it, the conversation started flowing. I got so caught up in the joy of it all that I accidentally let slip that my fiancé wanted to keep the engagement a secret from his family, which led to a bit of chatter from my family about how strange it was.

The next day, my boyfriend found out that I had mentioned his wish for secrecy and was furious. He felt I had betrayed his trust and put him in an awkward position with his family. I tried to explain that I didn’t think it was a big deal and that it was just family excitement, but he was still upset. Now, he’s been distant and hasn’t really spoken to me about it.

I feel terrible, but I also believe that our engagement is something to be celebrated, and I didn’t think keeping it a secret was healthy for our relationship. AITA for mentioning his desire for secrecy during the family dinner?

I (28F) recently moved in with my partner (30M) after dating for a couple of years. We were both really excited about this new chapter and spent a lot of time decorating and setting up our cozy little home. However, there's been a bit of tension lately over a specific issue regarding my cat, Luna.

Luna is a rescue cat I've had for about five years. She's incredibly shy and has a history of trauma, so she can be a bit skittish around new people and loud noises. My partner is generally understanding, but he has a few friends who come over regularly and love to bring their dogs with them. I made it clear before we moved in together that I wasn't comfortable with dogs in the house, especially since Luna is not used to them and could feel threatened.

Last week, my partner decided to invite his friends over for a game night without telling me. I came home to find two large dogs running around our apartment, barking and jumping, and Luna was nowhere to be found. I panicked, searching every nook and cranny for her, and finally found her hiding under the bed, trembling. I was furious and confronted my partner about it. He said he thought it would be fine since the dogs are friendly and he didn't think Luna would mind.

I expressed how violated I felt that he would disregard my wishes and put Luna in such a stressful situation. He apologized but also argued that I was being overly dramatic and that it was "just a couple of dogs." He said I needed to be more flexible, especially since it was his home too.

Since then, there's been a bit of a cold war between us. I haven’t talked to him much, and he’s been giving me the silent treatment in return. Friends have told me I’m justified in being upset, but my partner thinks I’m being unreasonable. 

AITA for being upset about my partner inviting dogs over without my permission and putting my cat in a stressful situation?

For context, I (F, 28) recently moved back to my hometown after living in a bigger city for a few years. I was excited to reconnect with old friends, especially my best friend from high school, Sarah (F, 28). We used to be inseparable, but life got in the way, and we drifted apart.

AITA for mentioning my past wedding plans at my friend's engagement party?

I (28F) recently got married to my husband (30M) after being together for five years. We had a small, intimate wedding with just family and close friends, and it was a beautiful day. However, there’s been some drama since then, and I’m feeling conflicted about my feelings.

For context, I'm a 28-year-old woman and I’ve recently moved back to my hometown after living in a different city for several years. For context, I (F, 28) recently got engaged to my fiancé (M, 30) after being together for five years. We have a good relationship, but we have different views on family dynamics. So, I (30F) recently had a bit of a conflict with my sister (28F) that’s left me wondering if I’m the one in the wrong.

I love Sarah, but I told her I wasn't really comfortable having someone stay over for an indefinite period. My place is small, and I value my alone time after living with my family for so long.

She seemed disappointed but said she understood. A few days later, she texted me saying that her upstairs neighbors were being particularly loud and offered to come over and hang out instead. I agreed, thinking it would be nice to have company. However, when she arrived, she brought a suitcase with her and announced that she was going to stay the night to "escape the noise." 

I hesitated but didn't want to seem rude, so I let her stay. The next morning, she was still there, lounging around, and I felt uncomfortable. I had work to do, and she was just watching TV and eating my snacks. I gently reminded her that I really needed my space, and she seemed to take it the wrong way, saying things like, “I thought we were friends and could support each other.” 

Finally, after a couple more days of her hanging out uninvited, I told her that she needed to find a different place to stay. I explained that I appreciated her company, but I needed my home to be my own again. She got upset and said I was being selfish and unsupportive during a tough time.

Now I’m feeling guilty and wondering if I was being too harsh. AITA for asking my friend to leave my apartment?

So I (28F) have a younger brother (22M) who recently got engaged to his girlfriend (23F) after dating for about eight months. We’re a close family, and I love my brother, but honestly, I was shocked when he announced the engagement. It felt rushed, and I didn’t think they really knew each other that well yet. 

A few weeks ago, my brother asked me to be the maid of honor. At first, I was flattered, but then I realized it meant I’d have to help plan the wedding, which is something I’ve never done before. I was nervous but agreed, thinking that maybe this would help me bond with his fiancée and get to know her better.

About a week into the planning, my brother and his fiancée had a disagreement over the guest list. She wanted to invite a ton of people, most of whom my brother had never met. He was feeling overwhelmed, and while I was trying to be supportive, I couldn’t help but voice my opinion that maybe they should keep it smaller, especially since they didn’t have a huge budget. 

Well, my brother took my suggestion as being dismissive of his fiancée’s wishes, and he ended up getting really upset with me. He accused me of trying to take control of the wedding planning and undermining their decisions. I tried to explain that I was just trying to help, but he wouldn’t listen. 

A few days later, I overheard my brother telling his fiancée that he didn’t want to work with me on the planning anymore because I was “too negative.” I felt crushed because I genuinely care about them both and just wanted the best for their wedding. 

After some thought, I decided to step back and let them plan the wedding without my input. However, when I told them I wouldn’t be involved anymore, my brother exploded at me, saying that I was ruining everything and that I should’ve been the supportive sister instead of criticizing. 

Now I’m left wondering if I was too harsh in expressing my feelings or if I was right to prioritize my brother’s happiness over my desire to be involved. AITA for stepping back from the wedding planning?

I (28F) recently got married, and my sister (30F) was my maid of honor. We’ve always been close, but things have been tense since the wedding. Here’s the background: My sister has been in a serious relationship with her boyfriend for about two years. They’ve discussed getting married, but there hasn’t been an official proposal yet. I’ve always supported her and encouraged her to take her time, but she’s made some comments about feeling “left behind” because I got married first.

During my wedding planning, I made it clear to everyone, including my sister, that I wanted a small, intimate ceremony with only our closest family and friends. I thought we were on the same page, but when I sent out the invites, she texted me that she thought it was unfair that I didn’t include her boyfriend. I explained that my wedding wasn’t the right setting for people who weren’t immediate family or in the wedding party, and I felt that having him there might take away from the day.

Fast forward to the wedding day. My sister showed up with her boyfriend, even though she knew I didn’t want him there. I was upset, but I didn’t say anything at the moment. I figured it was my day, and I didn’t want to create a scene. However, after the wedding, when I was expressing my feelings about how it went, I mentioned that I wished she had respected my wishes since I’d been upfront about wanting it to be intimate. She got defensive and said I was being selfish and that I was acting like my wedding was more important than her feelings.

Now she’s not speaking to me, and our parents are saying I overreacted and should have just accepted that she brought her boyfriend. I feel like I stood my ground on my wedding day and that it was my right to make the call on the guest list. AITA for feeling upset about my sister's decision to bring her boyfriend and for expecting her to respect my wishes?

I (28F) recently graduated and landed my first job, which I’m really excited about. I’ve always been close with my younger brother (20M), and since he’s still in college, I thought it would be a great opportunity for us to live together for a bit. We found a small apartment, and I’m paying the bulk of the rent since I have a stable income.

At first, things were going smoothly. I set some ground rules—like keeping the common areas clean and not having parties on weekdays. I also asked him to contribute to groceries, but we agreed that I would cover most of that since I could afford it better.

However, things have started to unravel lately. My brother has been inviting his friends over, and they’ve turned our living room into a hangout zone, which is fine occasionally but it’s becoming a regular thing. I’ve come home to find the place completely trashed and my brother just shrugging it off. 

Last week, I came home after a long day to find that they’d spilled soda all over the couch and there were half-empty pizza boxes everywhere. I lost my cool and told him that this wasn't acceptable and that he needs to take responsibility for his actions and clean up after his friends. He got defensive and claimed I was being "overly dramatic" and that it was just a "normal college vibe."

I ended up telling him that if this continues, I’d have to reconsider our living arrangement. He got upset and said I was being a controlling sister who couldn’t handle him having a social life. I didn’t mean to threaten our living situation, but I feel like I’m being taken for granted here.

Now he’s been giving me the cold shoulder, and I’m starting to feel guilty. Maybe I should’ve handled it differently? AITA for wanting him to be more responsible as a roommate?

For context, I (F, 28) am a teacher at an elementary school, and I have a close-knit group of colleagues that I usually socialize with outside of work. One of my coworkers, “Sarah” (F, 30), is particularly close to me and has been going through a rough patch with her partner. She often comes to me for advice and support.

I encouraged her to take time for herself and to consider her options carefully. However, I also made it clear that I felt she deserved better than to be treated that way.

Fast forward a couple of weeks, and Sarah eventually decided to break up with him. I was proud of her for standing up for herself and supported her through the process. However, I accidentally let it slip in a group chat with another coworker, “Jess” (F, 27), that Sarah was going through a breakup and mentioned that it was due to infidelity. The following week, Sarah reached out to me, clearly upset. She had found out that Jess had mentioned the breakup to some others in the staff room, turning it into a bit of gossip. I tried to explain that I didn’t mean for it to spread, and I thought Jess was a trustworthy person, but I still feel terrible that I let it slip in the first place.

Now, Sarah is distancing herself from me, and I feel like I’ve ruined our friendship. I apologized and offered to talk it through, but she hasn’t responded positively. I’m starting to wonder if I messed up by not being more careful with her private information. AITA for mentioning Sarah’s breakup in a group chat?

So, I (28F) recently got married, and my husband (30M) and I decided to have a small, intimate wedding ceremony with only close family and friends present. Due to the current state of the world, we prioritized the health and safety of our guests, and it was really important to us to keep it under 50 people.

A few weeks before the wedding, my sister (26F) announced that she had a friend who would be in town and wanted to come to the wedding. I told her we were only inviting close family and that we really needed to keep the numbers down. My sister insisted that this friend was like family to her and "needed to be there." I stood my ground and told her it wasn't personal, but we couldn't accommodate her friend.

Fast forward to the wedding day. My sister shows up with her friend, completely disregarding our request. I was shocked and really hurt, but I didn’t want to ruin the day, so I tried to brush it off. However, I couldn't help but feel that my sister had disrespected our wishes.

After the ceremony, I confronted my sister and told her that she shouldn’t have brought her friend and that it felt like a betrayal. She got defensive, saying that I was being too controlling and that she just wanted to share the day with someone important to her. I ended up asking her to leave, which led to a huge blow-up between us. She stormed out in tears and hasn’t spoken to me since.

Now, my parents are saying I overreacted and should have just let it go. I feel like I was justified in wanting to maintain the integrity of our guest list. AITA for asking my sister to leave my wedding because she brought someone I specifically said not to invite?

So, I (F, 35) live in a small town where everyone knows each other, and I own a local coffee shop. I’ve been running my business for about five years now, and it has been my dream to create a warm, welcoming space for the community. Recently, I decided to host a weekly open mic night for local talents to showcase their skills, which has been a great success. 

Last week, a musician (M, 28) who’s been coming every week asked if he could bring a few friends to perform. I agreed, thinking it would be fun to have more acts. However, when he showed up, I was surprised to see a large group of about ten people with him. I didn’t want to turn them away, so I let them stay, but I made it clear that I couldn't accommodate such a big group every week. 

As the evening progressed, things got out of hand. They were loud, dominating the stage, and even started charging people for their merchandise without my permission. I politely asked them to tone it down and reminded them that this was meant to be a supportive environment for everyone, not just them. The musician got defensive and argued that they were just trying to promote their music. Eventually, I had to cut their set short and ask them to leave, which caused a scene.

The next day, I received a message from the musician claiming I was “killing local art” and “not supporting the community.” A few friends of his also reached out to me, saying I was being unreasonable and that I should’ve let them perform longer since they brought in more people. 

Now, I’m feeling torn. I want to support local talent, but I also have to maintain the atmosphere and rules of my business. My regular customers were uncomfortable with the noise and chaos, and I don’t want to lose them either. 

AITA for asking the group to leave and enforcing my original agreement?

So, I (F, 28) have a 6-year-old son, Jake. About a year ago, I started dating Steve (M, 30). Steve has been great with Jake, and they've developed a solid bond. However, there's something that’s been bothering me lately.

She rolled her eyes and said I was being "too uptight."

The next visit, Emily brought a gift for Jake - a toy that was meant for older children. I thanked her but explained that I didn’t want him to have it because it wasn't suitable for his age. After that, I had a conversation with Steve about how I felt Emily wasn’t respecting my boundaries as a parent. He seemed to understand but asked me to be more forgiving, saying that she loves Jake and just wants to connect with him. Last weekend, I had a small birthday party for Jake and invited close family and friends. I didn’t invite Emily because I didn’t want the chaos of her trying to take over the situation. I (29F) recently had a major falling out with my sister (27F) over what I thought was a simple family gathering. For some background, our family has a tradition of celebrating birthdays with a big dinner. This year, my sister’s birthday and my birthday were only a week apart, so I suggested we combine the celebrations to save time and effort. My sister was initially on board, but as the date approached, she started making demands. She wanted her birthday to be the main event and insisted that we celebrate her with a cake and gifts while my birthday should just be a side note. I agreed to this, thinking it was her special day, but then she started telling me who could and couldn't come. She didn't want our cousin, who I’m close with, to come because they had a falling out last year. I thought that was unfair and brought it up to her, but she brushed me off.

The night of the combined dinner arrived, and my sister ended up being late because she was getting her hair done. I was stressed because I had spent hours cooking, and I wanted everything to be perfect. When she finally showed up, she was upset that I hadn’t made her favorite dish. I told her I had to make compromises and that I thought we both agreed on the menu. She exploded, saying I had ruined her birthday by not dedicating the entire evening to her. 

Things escalated when, during the cake cutting, she made a big show out of pretending my birthday didn't exist. She blew out her candles and then turned to me and said, “Maybe next year you can have your own party.” I felt humiliated and made a sarcastic comment about how great it must be to be the center of attention. 

After that, she stormed off and hasn’t spoken to me since. Our parents think I was being insensitive and should have just let her have the spotlight. I feel like I was trying to be accommodating, but now I’m questioning whether I handled it poorly. AITA for wanting to celebrate both our birthdays together and for my reaction when she disregarded my own birthday?

For context, I’m a 28-year-old woman and I’ve been dating my boyfriend, who is 30, for about two years. We both have full-time jobs and lead pretty busy lives, but we always carve out time for each other on weekends.

I've been living in a small apartment (F, 28) with my roommate (M, 29) for about two years now. We both have busy work lives and tend to keep to ourselves. Recently, he started dating this girl who is really sweet but has a bit of a habit that I find pretty annoying. 

She’s been coming over a lot, which is fine, but she always brings her dog with her. I’m not against dogs or anything, but my roommate’s girlfriend’s dog is a large breed and pretty hyperactive. Whenever she’s over, the dog runs around the apartment, jumps on the furniture, and even knocks over my plants. I’ve tried to be patient because I understand it’s a new relationship and they want to spend time together, but it’s becoming too much.

I reached out to my roommate and expressed my concerns. I told him I’m uncomfortable with the dog in our space all the time because it’s damaging my belongings and I worry about my safety since I’m not used to being around such a large, energetic dog. I suggested they either leave the dog at her place or take it for walks during their visits. He got defensive and said that I was being unreasonable and that it’s just a dog, not a monster. He also mentioned that the dog is part of her life, and he doesn’t want to make her choose between him and her pet.

Feeling frustrated, I set a boundary and told him that if his girlfriend’s dog continues to come over frequently, I would consider looking for a new place to live. Now both him and his girlfriend are upset with me, and I'm feeling guilty since I know it’s a tough situation for him. But I also feel like I deserve to have a comfortable living environment.

I (28F) recently had a confrontation with my sister (26F) over her behavior during family gatherings, and I’m not sure if I overreacted. For context, our family is pretty close, and we have a tradition of hosting Sunday dinners at our parents' house. We've been doing this since we were kids, and it’s a great time for everyone to catch up.

However, my sister has developed a habit of bringing her boyfriend (27M) to these dinners despite the fact that he’s kind of a jerk. He’s rude to my parents, makes sarcastic comments about their cooking, and seems disinterested in interacting with anyone. Last week, he made a joke about how "it's a wonder any of us survived our childhood with the food our parents served." After the dinner, I texted my sister about how uncomfortable I felt her boyfriend was making everyone, and I suggested that maybe she should consider leaving him at home for the next gathering. I never told her to break up with him—just to be mindful of how he’s affecting the atmosphere. She completely flipped out on me, saying that I was trying to control her relationship and that I should be more tolerant because “everyone deserves to be included, even if they’re not perfect.”

I (28F) recently moved into a new apartment, which I’m sharing with my college friend (29M). We’ve known each other for over a decade, and I thought living together would be great since we get along well. However, things have taken a weird turn.
