The breaking point came last week. I had a small gathering for my birthday and invited a few close friends. I spent the whole day cleaning and prepping, wanting everything to be perfect. The day of the party, I came home to find that my friend had invited some of his friends over without telling me, and they were all sitting in the living room. Not only that, but they had brought snacks that they didn't bother to clean up afterwards. I was shocked and upset because this wasn’t what I envisioned for my birthday celebration.

After my friends left, I confronted him about it. I expressed my frustration, saying that it felt disrespectful to have people over uninvited, especially when I had put in so much effort. He brushed it off, saying I was overreacting and that it was just a casual get-together. He even went on to say that I needed to “lighten up” about things.

Since then, there’s been this awkward tension in our apartment. He barely talks to me, and when he does, it feels forced. I’m beginning to wonder if I overreacted. Was it unreasonable for me to expect him to respect my wishes about having guests over, especially on a day that was special to me? AITA for getting upset about my friend inviting people over for my birthday?

I (28F) recently moved into a new apartment in a city where I don't know many people. My best friend (29F) lives about an hour away, and she was excited to come visit me during the first week I moved in. I was thrilled to have her over, as it gets pretty lonely in a new place.

Before she arrived, I spent a lot of time cleaning, decorating, and even stocked up on some snacks and drinks. I wanted to make it special since it was her first time seeing my new home. When she finally came over, we had a great time catching up and reminiscing about our old college days.

However, things started to take a turn when she began to critique my apartment. She pointed out that my furniture was "cheap," my decor was "tacky," and that I should have chosen "better colors" for the walls. At first, I brushed it off, thinking she was just joking. But then, she started suggesting that I should just "get rid of everything" and "start over," which honestly hurt my feelings. I worked hard to make this place feel like home on a tight budget, and I was proud of what I had accomplished.

Later, while we were in the kitchen, she casually mentioned that I should "invite her over next time when I have better things to show off." I felt my heart sink. I told her that it wasn't about impressing anyone and that I just wanted to create a cozy space for myself. She laughed it off, but I could tell she didn't really get where I was coming from.

After that, I started to feel annoyed and distant. Towards the end of her visit, I told her that I appreciated her honesty, but I needed her to be more supportive instead of critical. She seemed surprised and hurt, saying she was just trying to help me improve my living space. I ended up asking her to leave because I felt overwhelmed.

Now, she's upset with me and thinks I overreacted. I feel bad for hurting her feelings, but I also believe that friends should uplift each other, not tear each other down, especially during a vulnerable time like moving. I (28F) am in a bit of a dilemma and could really use some outside perspective on whether I’m in the wrong here.

For context, I'm a 28-year-old woman and I’ve recently moved back to my hometown after living in a different city for several years. I decided to throw a small housewarming party and invited some old friends, including my childhood friend Sarah, who has a 3-year-old son. Sarah and I have been friends for over 20 years, but I’ve never really been close to her son.

On the day of the party, Sarah showed up with her son, despite my invitation specifying that it was an adult gathering. I felt guilty for saying it, but I reiterated that it would be better if she didn’t bring him along. She looked hurt and said she didn’t have anyone to watch him on short notice. AITA for not allowing my friend to bring her son to my adult-only housewarming party?

I (28F) have a younger sister, Leah (24F), who just got engaged to her boyfriend, Mark (26M). They’ve been dating for about two years, and honestly, I think they make a great couple. However, Leah has always had a tendency to be a bit of a bridezilla, and it seems to be getting worse.

So I (F, 28) recently got engaged to my fiancé (M, 30) after a really sweet proposal. We’ve been together for about 4 years, and I was so excited to start planning our wedding. However, my excitement quickly turned to frustration when my future mother-in-law (F, 60) decided to take charge.

For some context, I (28F) recently moved to a new city for a job opportunity. After that, I tried to be extra mindful of everything, but it was clear that no matter what I did, Jake was going to find something to complain about. So I (29F) have a younger brother (24M) who has always been a bit of a free spirit. He dropped out of college a couple of years ago and has been traveling and living off odd jobs ever since. While I admire his adventurous spirit, my parents and I have often worried about his lack of stability.

I (28F) recently had a pretty big falling out with my sister (26F). For some context, our parents have always favored her, and it’s been a sore spot for me for years. They don’t realize how much it affects me, but I’ve tried to keep the peace because, at the end of the day, she’s still my sister.

My sister, knowing it was my birthday, decided to invite herself and her boyfriend (who I don’t particularly like) without asking if it was okay first. I didn’t appreciate that she assumed she could just join in, but I figured it was fine since family is important, and it was my birthday.

I (28F) recently got engaged to my fiancé (30M), and we decided to have a small, intimate wedding ceremony with just our closest friends and family. I'm (F) in my late 20s and recently got married to my husband (M), who has two kids from a previous relationship. For context, I (F, 28) have a younger brother (M, 22) who just graduated and moved back in with our parents while he looks for a job. I (29F) recently went through a tough breakup with my boyfriend (30M) of three years. We had planned on moving in together, but when he called it quits, I had to quickly find a new place to live. Luckily, my friend (28F) offered me a room in her apartment while I got back on my feet. I really appreciated her generosity.

Things started off great, but soon, I noticed she would make comments about my cooking. I love to cook, and I tend to experiment with new recipes. The first time I made a spicy curry, she said, “Wow, that smells strong. Are you sure that’s a good idea?” I shrugged it off, but the comments kept coming. “Do you really think that’s healthy?” or “I guess some people like things like that.” 

I started to feel self-conscious about what I was making, but I tried not to let it get to me. Then, one evening, I made a big batch of homemade chili and invited her to join me. She accepted but when she took a bite, she immediately grimaced and said, “Wow, you must really like it spicy! I can’t handle this.” I didn’t take it personally; I offered her some sour cream to tone it down, but she just pushed her bowl away and said, “No thanks, I think I’ll just stick to my salad.”

The next day, I got a text from her saying she couldn’t keep living with me if I was going to keep cooking such “strong-smelling” food. I was taken aback. I understood that living in close quarters means being considerate, but I felt like she was being overly critical. I suggested we could work on a cooking schedule where I’d cook on certain days and she could stick to her salads on others, but she didn’t like that idea. 

Now, I’ve decided to look for a new place, but I’m starting to wonder if I’m the one in the wrong for cooking what I enjoy in her space. She’s been my friend for years, and I feel bad that it’s come to this. AITA for cooking what I like in my friend’s apartment?

I (29F) recently moved into a new apartment and have been super excited to finally have my own space. I’m a big fan of cooking, and I often try out new recipes that can get a bit messy. My best friend (30F) has been living in the area for a while and has always expressed her love for my cooking, often asking for me to make her stuff when she visits.

I tried to be patient and just let it slide, but then I found my favorite cooking oil empty and she casually mentioned that she used it for a recipe she tried without telling me. 

On the third day, I planned to make a special dinner for us, but when I checked the fridge, I found that she had used most of my ingredients without asking. So, I (28F) have a younger brother, Jake (21M), who has recently started dating a girl named Sarah (20F). They’ve been together for about six months now, and while I think she’s sweet, I’ve noticed that she seems to be pretty insecure about their relationship.

For context, I (F, 28) recently moved into a new apartment after getting a promotion at work. I (30F) recently got married to my partner (32M) after dating for five years. We had a small wedding ceremony with close friends and family, and it was a beautiful day. However, there's been a lot of drama surrounding the event, mainly because of my sister (28F).

I (28F) recently had a pretty heated disagreement with my sister (32F) and now I'm left wondering if I went too far.

I (29F) have a younger sister (23F) who is getting married next month. Last week, after we finally met the deadline, we had a team celebration planned. I’d arranged for pizza and drinks to thank everyone for their effort. However, one of my team members, “Tom,” who’s been with the company for about a year, showed up late and immediately started criticizing my management style in front of everyone, saying I was too demanding and made unnecessary changes that delayed the project. Jake, on the other hand, dropped out of college after a year and has been bouncing between odd jobs. He recently came to me asking for help. I told him that I think he should focus on getting his finances in order before thinking about a vacation, especially since he’s not contributing to household expenses.

Jake got really upset and said I was being a buzzkill and that he deserves to have fun too. I (28F) recently moved into a new apartment in a building where the majority of the tenants are older adults. I was pretty excited about my new place until I learned that the previous tenant had been a beloved member of the community who had passed away. Many of my neighbors still speak fondly of her, which is sweet, but it’s also created an atmosphere where I feel like I’m under a microscope.

A couple of weeks ago, I hosted a small housewarming gathering to celebrate my new place. I kept the guest list short, inviting just a few close friends. We kept the noise level down, but around 10 PM, an older neighbor knocked on my door. She seemed upset and told us that we were being too loud. I apologized and assured her we would keep it down.

I heard a knock again and opened the door to find another neighbor, a man in his 70s this time. He told me that I needed to stop making noise at night because it was disruptive. I was taken aback because it was a Friday night, and I didn’t think we were being unreasonable. I thanked him for letting me know and promised to be mindful.

The next morning, I received a text from the building manager saying that several tenants had complained about noise coming from my apartment. This felt really unfair, as I tried to keep things low-key. I shot a quick message to the group chat with my friends, joking about how I might have to start sending out noise complaint notices before any gathering. I thought it was funny, but one of my friends suggested I should apologize to the neighbors and maybe even invite them over next time to show that I’m friendly. I brushed it off, but then I started to second-guess myself.

Was I being an inconsiderate neighbor for hosting any sort of gathering? I really didn’t think I was being loud, especially during reasonable hours, but now I’m wondering if I’m the one in the wrong for not reaching out to them personally. AITA for wanting to enjoy my home without worrying about stepping on anyone's toes?

So I (28F) recently moved into a new apartment in a pretty tight-knit building. I’ve got a neighbor, let's call her Sarah (30sF), who seems nice enough, but we don’t know each other well yet. I’m a bit of an introvert, and I prefer to keep to myself, especially while settling in.

For context, I (F, 28) have a younger brother (M, 22) who just graduated and moved back in with our parents while he looks for a job. I (29F) recently went through a tough breakup with my boyfriend (30M) of three years. We had planned on moving in together, but when he called it quits, I had to quickly find a new place to live. The first time I made a spicy curry, she said, “Wow, that smells strong. Are you sure that’s a good idea?” I shrugged it off, but the comments kept coming. “Do you really think that’s healthy?” or “I guess some people like things like that.” 

I started to feel self-conscious about what I was making, but I tried not to let it get to me. Then, one evening, I made a big batch of homemade chili and invited her to join me. She accepted but when she took a bite, she immediately grimaced and said, “Wow, you must really like it spicy! I can’t handle this.” I didn’t take it personally; I offered her some sour cream to tone it down, but she just pushed her bowl away and said, “No thanks, I think I’ll just stick to my salad.”

I (29F) recently moved into a new apartment and have been super excited to finally have my own space. I’m a big fan of cooking, and I often try out new recipes that can get a bit messy. So, I (28F) have a younger brother, Jake (21M), who has recently started dating a girl named Sarah (20F). They’ve been together for about six months now, and while I think she’s sweet, I’ve noticed that she seems to be pretty insecure about their relationship.

I made it clear that he needed to return it on Sunday evening so I could use it for work on Monday morning.

Well, Sunday evening came and went, and I didn’t hear from him. I texted him multiple times, but he didn’t respond until late that night when he texted that they were still out of town and he’d be back the next day. I was frustrated but tried to be understanding, telling him that he really needed to let me know next time. He assured me he would be back by early afternoon.

Monday morning rolled around, and he still hadn't returned. I had to scramble to find a backup plan for getting to work. I finally got in touch with him around noon, and he said he was “on his way” but then sent me a video of him and his friends at a beach party. I lost my cool at that point and told him he was being irresponsible and that he disrespected my trust by not returning the car when he promised.

When he finally got back later that evening, I confronted him about it. He brushed off my concerns and said I was being dramatic. I ended up raising my voice and told him that he was acting like a child. He stormed off and hasn’t talked to me since.

Now, my parents are saying I overreacted and that I should apologize for yelling. I feel like I was justified in being upset and that he needed to understand the consequences of his actions. AITA for yelling at my brother over the car situation?

Recently, I found out that my brother is feeling pressured to please our parents and has decided to go ahead with a traditional wedding, which I know will stress him out. Here’s where things got complicated. I told him that my family usually has a big gathering with extended family, and I wasn't sure how they would feel about him being there since they’ve never met him before. He assured me that he would make a good impression and that he really wanted to be there.

However, last week, I found out that my mom has invited my ex-boyfriend (29M) to the holiday gathering, which is a huge deal because he and I had a pretty messy breakup. Recently, our parents decided to downsize and move to a smaller house, which means he can’t stay with them anymore. They asked me if I could take him in temporarily until he gets back on his feet.

I agreed, thinking it wouldn’t be a big deal. However, since he moved in a month ago, it’s been a nightmare. He leaves his dirty dishes in the sink for days, plays his music loudly at odd hours, and has a habit of “borrowing” my stuff without asking. I’ve tried talking to him about it, but he just brushes it off, claiming he’s “in the zone” for his music and that I should be more supportive.

Last week, I reached my limit when I came home to find my favorite guitar (which I’ve been very protective of) covered in sticky soda because he had a party while I was at work. I was furious. Instead of confronting him calmly, I ended up yelling at him about respecting my things and being an adult. He got defensive and said I was being too hard on him during a “vulnerable time.”

Now, he’s barely speaking to me, and our parents are upset because they think I should’ve been more understanding and supportive. They even said I should apologize to him for overreacting and that he’s going through a tough time. I feel like I’m stuck in the middle here—trying to help him while also wanting my space and belongings respected.

AITA for losing my temper and not being more supportive of my brother?

I'm a 28-year-old woman, and I've been living with my boyfriend, Jake, who's 30, for about a year. We both have decent jobs, and we split our bills fairly evenly. The only thing is, I tend to be a bit more meticulous about keeping our place clean than he is. I don’t mind doing most of the cleaning because I know it keeps our living space comfortable, but it gets frustrating when I feel like I’m doing it all.

Last week, I was having a rough day at work. I came home exhausted and just wanted to relax. When I walked in, the place was a disaster zone. Dishes piled up in the sink, clothes thrown everywhere, and the garbage was overflowing. I snapped a bit and told Jake that I needed him to start pulling his weight more when it comes to cleaning. He got defensive, saying that it’s not a big deal and that I’m making a mountain out of a molehill. I was really upset, and instead of listening to me, he just shut down and got silent.

The next day, I decided to take a different approach. I wrote him a note, listing out specific tasks I needed help with and put it on the fridge. I thought it was a good compromise and would make it easier for him to see what needed to be done without feeling overwhelmed. He came home, saw the note, and got really angry. He said I was treating him like a child and that if I wanted him to clean, I should just ask him instead of making a list.

Now we’re in a bit of a standoff. He hasn’t done any of the tasks on the list, and I feel like he’s being immature by refusing to clean out of spite. I’m just trying to make our home a better place to live. My friends say I should have just talked to him about it more calmly, but I feel like I have tried that before. 

AITA for writing the note instead of just asking him to clean?

So here’s the situation. I (28F) have a younger sister (24F) who has been dating this guy (26M) for about a year now. Initially, I wasn’t a fan of him because he seemed pretty self-centered and didn’t treat her the way I thought she deserved. However, I tried to keep my opinions to myself because she seemed happy.

Fast forward to a couple of months ago, and I found out he’s been openly making fun of her interests in front of her friends and family. For example, she loves anime and cosplay, and he jokingly called her “cringe” in front of us during dinner. It made her visibly uncomfortable, and I could tell it hurt her feelings. I didn’t say anything at the time, but it stuck with me.

Last weekend, we had a family barbecue, and my sister was super excited to show off her latest cosplay outfit she had been working on. When she walked in, he made another snarky comment about how she looked “ridiculous” and that he hoped she wasn’t going to embarrass herself. I couldn’t take it anymore. I calmly told him that he needed to stop making fun of her and that it was really not cool to belittle her hobbies, especially when she put so much effort into them.

He got defensive and laughed it off, saying I was “overreacting” and that it was just his sense of humor. My sister looked conflicted but didn't say anything, which made me feel even worse. After the barbecue, I reached out to her privately and told her that I was there for her if she wanted to talk about her relationship. She seemed grateful but told me I shouldn’t have said anything to him because it made things awkward.

Now I’m feeling guilty. Maybe I shouldn’t have intervened, even though I hate seeing her with someone who doesn’t respect her. But I also feel like I stood up for my sister in a situation where she might not have felt comfortable doing so herself. 

So, AITA for calling out my sister’s boyfriend for making fun of her?

I (28F) recently got engaged to my long-time boyfriend (30M). We’ve been together for almost six years, and we’re both super excited to take this next step in our lives. However, there's an issue that’s been weighing on me, and I really need some outside perspective on whether I’m being unreasonable.

A few weeks ago, my fiancé and I hosted an engagement party at our apartment, inviting friends and family to celebrate with us. It was a great evening filled with laughter, food, and drinks. During the party, my fiancé’s sister (27F) showed up unannounced with her two young kids (ages 4 and 6). We had a full house already, and I had explicitly told my fiancé that I wanted a more intimate gathering without kids, mainly because we wanted to keep the focus on us and celebrate our engagement with friends.

While I adore my future sister-in-law and her kids, I felt overwhelmed by their presence and the chaos they brought. It was hard to have meaningful conversations, and I felt like my vision for the night was compromised. To make matters worse, the kids were running around, spilling drinks, and knocking into things. At one point, one of them almost knocked over a family heirloom that I cherish.

I politely asked my fiancé to talk to his sister about keeping the kids more subdued, but he shrugged it off, saying they were just having fun. Eventually, I lost my cool and told my fiancé that I was really frustrated about the situation and that I needed him to step in and set some boundaries. He ended up getting upset with me for bringing it up during the party and said I was being too harsh on his sister.

Now, his sister is upset with me, claiming I made her feel unwelcome, and my fiancé is caught in the middle. I feel guilty about how I handled the situation, but at the same time, I believe I had valid concerns about our engagement celebration. I didn’t intend to hurt anyone’s feelings; I just wanted the night to go as I had envisioned.

So, AITA for being upset that my fiancé's sister brought her kids to our engagement party despite my wishes?

For some context, I (28F) recently moved to a new city for a job opportunity. My best friend, Sarah (27F), has been living here for a few years and offered me to crash at her apartment while I settled in. I was grateful for the gesture, especially since I didn't have anything lined up in terms of housing.

Sarah has a roommate, Jake (30M), who I've known casually for a few years. When I moved in, I made sure to respect their space and kept my things to a minimum. However, I quickly realized that Jake was not as pleasant as I thought. He’s a neat freak, which I can appreciate to an extent, but he started getting increasingly critical about everything – from the way I left the kitchen to how I organized my stuff in the shared bathroom.

It all came to a head when he confronted me about my laundry. I was doing a small load of clothes, and he absolutely flipped out because I used the washing machine during “peak hours.” He insisted that I should have waited until later and even went so far as to say I was “disrupting their household routine.” I was taken aback because I thought it was a pretty reasonable time to do laundry, especially since I was living there temporarily.

After that, I tried to be extra mindful of everything, but it was clear that no matter what I did, Jake was going to find something to complain about. One day, he texted me about a “cleaning schedule” that I wasn’t aware of and demanded that I follow it strictly. I finally lost my patience and told him that I’m only staying for a couple of months and that he needed to chill out. 

That night, Sarah came home and I could tell she had been talking to Jake. She said I needed to be more considerate because Jake was feeling “overwhelmed” by my presence in their space. I tried to explain my side, but she seemed to side with him. I decided it was best to find my own place sooner rather than later, which I did within a few days.

Now, Sarah is upset with me for “causing drama” between her and her roommate and said that I should have just tried harder to accommodate Jake. I feel like I was being reasonable and just standing up for myself. AITA for not wanting to endure Jake’s antics and deciding to move out?

So I (29F) have a younger brother (24M) who has always been a bit of a free spirit. He dropped out of college a couple of years ago and has been traveling and living off odd jobs ever since. While I admire his adventurous spirit, my parents and I have often worried about his lack of stability. 

Recently, he reached out to me, asking if he could stay at my apartment for a month while he figures things out. I live in a small one-bedroom place and generally like my space, but I agreed because I want to support him. However, I laid down some ground rules: no loud music late at night, no guests over without asking, and he needs to help with chores since I work full-time.

The first week was fine, but then he started breaking the rules. He had friends over multiple times, playing music loudly, and I found out he wasn’t cleaning up after himself. I confronted him about it, and he promised to do better, but it didn’t change much. I came home one night after a long day at work to find my apartment a mess and a group of his friends hanging out.

I lost my temper and told him that if he couldn’t respect my space and the rules I set, he would need to find another place to stay. He got defensive and accused me of being unsupportive and inflexible. I felt bad afterward because I know he’s going through a tough time, but I also feel like I deserve to have my home treated with respect.

Now, my parents think I overreacted and should have given him more chances. They argue that he’s my brother and needs my support right now. I can see their point, but I also think I have to stand up for my own needs.

AITA for kicking him out after just a few weeks?

For context, I (F, 28) recently got engaged to my boyfriend (M, 30) after being together for four years. We’re both excited, but there’s been some tension brewing around the wedding planning process. My fiancé has a younger sister (F, 22) who is a great person, but she has a habit of being very self-centered. She was excited when we announced our engagement and immediately started talking about how she wants to be the Maid of Honor, even though she hasn't even asked me if I want her to be.

During a family dinner this past weekend, she started suggesting that we have a huge wedding and wanted to know if I’d be okay with her picking out my dress. I thought it was a little much, especially since I have my own vision for the wedding. I told her I appreciate her enthusiasm but that I want to be involved in all the decisions about the wedding, including my dress. She seemed offended but said, “Okay, okay! I’ll just help you pick out the dress!”

I thought it was settled, but then she started posting on social media about how she can't wait to plan my wedding. I felt uncomfortable because it made it seem like she was taking over, and it’s MY wedding. So, I brought it up to my fiancé. He agreed with me that I should have the final say and that it’s important to set boundaries. 

I decided to sit down with her and calmly tell her that while I appreciate her excitement, I really want to have more control over the wedding planning process. I told her it’s my big day, and I want to make sure it reflects my and my fiancé's vision. She got really upset and accused me of being selfish and "not letting her be a part of something special."

Now, the rest of the family is divided. My fiancé thinks I did the right thing, but my future mother-in-law is upset and thinks I should let her help more. My own parents are supportive of me standing my ground, but I feel guilty about hurting her feelings. AITA for telling my future sister-in-law that I want to take charge of my wedding planning?

I (28F) recently had a pretty big falling out with my sister (26F). For some context, our parents have always favored her, and it’s been a sore spot for me for years. They don’t realize how much it affects me, but I’ve tried to keep the peace because, at the end of the day, she’s still my sister.

Last week was my birthday, and I was really excited about it. I planned a small get-together with close friends at my apartment. I bought decorations, made food, and even ordered a cake that I was really looking forward to. I sent out invites in advance and clearly stated that I wanted a low-key celebration.

My sister, knowing it was my birthday, decided to invite herself and her boyfriend (who I don’t particularly like) without asking if it was okay first. I didn’t appreciate that she assumed she could just join in, but I figured it was fine since family is important, and it was my birthday. 

The day of the party, she shows up with her boyfriend, and they brought a bunch of her friends along who I didn’t invite. The vibe shifted immediately. My friends felt uncomfortable because they didn't know anyone else, and her friends started taking over the music and food.

Things got worse when my sister insisted on doing a toast for me, which turned into her making it all about her. She started talking about how much she’s done for me over the years, how I should be grateful for having her as a sister, and that I should be more appreciative of our parents’ love for her. It felt like a punch to the gut on what was supposed to be my special day. 

I finally lost my cool and told her that it was my birthday, and if she wanted to make everything about her, she could leave. She got upset and stormed out with her friends, and now she’s been texting me saying I’m a terrible sister and ruined her night as well. 

I feel bad for how it ended, but I also think it’s unfair for her to take over my birthday and turn it into something it wasn’t supposed to be. I just wanted a nice evening with my friends. AITA for kicking my sister out on my birthday?
